correctness.rationale: For r≥3, q≥2, 1≤c<q, the orthogonal product projection of a binary block is exact and has cost F(k). F is strictly convex, so at every maximizing hypersimplex vertex all but at most one block are full or empty, uniquely determining the occupancy multiset from rc=aq+s. To classify continuous maximizers, the squared-distance variance inequality forces convex-combination constituent vertices to have equal maximal residuals; nonzero partial-block residuals distinguish vertices unless s=c, when the partial block has exactly zero residual. The resulting disjoint Δ(c,q) coordinate faces and isolated-vertex alternatives, with exact multiplicities, follow. Independent exact rational enumeration checked 37,986 occupancy profiles and arithmetic resonances for bounded parameters; it is not the all-parameter proof.
